newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen consolidating after EMU developments.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen consolidating after EMU developments.

text.p: Bunds were expected to trade in narrow ranges on Tuesday with a dearth of economic news on the schedule and many traders worried about the next turn in preperations for monetary union.
In early trade, the DTB September Bund future was up four basis points at 100.80, having traded in an early range between 100.63 and 100.85.

The only major event on the calendar came earlier this morning when the Federal Statistics Office said German consumer prices climbed 1.6 percent in May from the same month the year before. CPI had climbed 1.4 percent in April.
Traders said the market is now focused on developments in Paris where the French government has asked for time to consider its agreement to the stability pact.
Analysts said they see little room for Finance Minister Theo Waigel to make any changes to the pact that would favour employment over monetary stability as some fear the French may be pushing for.
"The market has only one thing on its mind," one trader said. "Is EMU coming or not."
The benchmark cash 10-year Bund climbed to 101.64 from 101.47 to yield 5.77 percent.
Traders said that with little else to focus on, they may consider moving down the yield curve into shorter maturity debt.
The yield curve was little changed in early trade with the spread between two- and 10-year maturities at 232 basis points.
They said they expected the Bund future to trade between 100.50 and 101.00 points on the day. The contract has good chart support with the 200-day moving average 100.50.
